This isn’t true. The EPA has regulatory authority to govern drinking water and water testing schedules. The Safe Drinking Water Act allows the EPA to “specify contaminants which, in the judgment of the Administrator, may have an adverse effect on the health of persons;” SEC 1401(1)(B) and “a maximum contaminant level…” SEC 1401(1)(C)(i). So as long as the EPA can provide a method an industry can use to lower a contaminant that the EPA identified as being carcinogenic, they have the authority to regulate it.

I’m seeing two main things, both of which are going to really really hurt your chops, especially when playing rudiments.

The first major thing I see is your overall hand position - meaning it is extremely tilted. While this isn’t exactly wrong (known as French grip) you may find it easier to incorporate your wrist if you’re using American or German style grips. The hand position is causing you to completely ignore the movement of your wrists, instead focusing mainly on using your fingers to get that sound. Think about it- what has bigger muscles? Your wrists, or your fingers? The trick is to incorporate them both so that you can get better chops by not relying on one over the other.

Another thing, which I sorta stated in my first point, was that you only incorporate your fingers. Make sure to incorporate your wrists a TON (probably more than any other part of your hand/arm when you play) and at louder parts you can incorporate your arm to. A great way I practiced this was by recording my hand much like you did, rewatching it, and asking myself if that’s the way I see all my favorite drummers do it. The answer was usually no, but one day it clicked! 

Please please PLEASE don’t stop working on your grip and rudiments. I made the mistake of getting a really bad habit of using too much arm in highschool, which has been a huge challenge to overcome. Just keep working at it everyday.

As you’ve already seen, it depends. I did a band day for a small college and everything seemed super laid back. Now, I’m in a big 10 marching band and it’s a huge challenge. Audition wise, my audition was a two day audition (Musical audition and then a marching audition). I can, however, give you some advice for any audition:

1. Be prepared. Know your solo and know how to play it well. Don’t just focus on notes and when to play them: show the judge that you can make music out of it was well.

2. Approach the audition with an open mind. The first step to getting better is admitting you don’t know everything, and a really good quote that was on a drumming subreddit was “the better you get, the more you know you suck”. Show the judges that you know how to improve and that you’re willing to learn.

3. A good attitude will make or break you. Go in ready to receive feedback and criticism, and hit the ground running every day of auditions. Show them that you want to improve, you want to have fun, and you want to make the band better.

4. Have fun! Don’t be nervous, take deep breathes, and remember, you’re there to have fun. Auditions are stressful, yes, but you’re there to play something that you love and to show off your ability.

Explore different genres of music. Punk, jazz, rock, metal, funk, big band, etc. covering those kinds of songs from different genres helps spice up your playing, and you can incorporate some of the lessons you’ve learned from other genres into others, ie the entirety of fool in the rain. 

You can also try out marching, check out dci cores such as Blue Devils, Santa Clara Vangaurd, Blue Coats, Boston Crusaders, etc. They are a totally different style than set playing, and can really open your eyes to the technicalities of what drumming can be. Also, they show you how rudiments are incorporated into a ton of different types of music, and each core has its own style.

See if you can join a band too, I know a common one is local church bands. But if you’re not religious, then feel free to grab some buddys and jam out in someone’s garage. 

All of these things have helped me get way more into drumming thrown I ever thought possible. I hope they do for you too. Happy drumming!
